To compute \( P^2 \), we need to multiply the transition matrix \( P \) by itself. The transition matrix given is:

\[
P = \begin{bmatrix}
0.5 & 0.5 \\
0.2 & 0.8
\end{bmatrix}
\]

We will compute \( P^2 = P \times P \):

\[
P^2 = \begin{bmatrix}
0.5 & 0.5 \\
0.2 & 0.8
\end{bmatrix}
\times
\begin{bmatrix}
0.5 & 0.5 \\
0.2 & 0.8
\end{bmatrix}
\]

To perform the multiplication, we calculate each entry as follows:

1. For the entry in the first row, first column:
\[
(0.5 \times 0.5) + (0.5 \times 0.2) = 0.25 + 0.1 = 0.35
\]

2. For the entry in the first row, second column:
\[
(0.5 \times 0.5) + (0.5 \times 0.8) = 0.25 + 0.4 = 0.65
\]

3. For the entry in the second row, first column:
\[
(0.2 \times 0.5) + (0.8 \times 0.2) = 0.1 + 0.16 = 0.26
\]

4. For the entry in the second row, second column:
\[
(0.2 \times 0.5) + (0.8 \times 0.8) = 0.1 + 0.64 = 0.74
\]

Putting these results together, we obtain:

\[
P^2 = \begin{bmatrix}
0.35 & 0.65 \\
0.26 & 0.74
\end{bmatrix}
\]

Final answer: \(\begin{bmatrix} 0.35 & 0.65 \\ 0.26 & 0.74 \end{bmatrix}\)
